title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-04-28
content:
Applied ML weekly notes - 2026-04-28

Attendees: Aisha Kapoor (owner), Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez, Diego Alvarez, Noor Patel (observability)
Meeting length: 45m

High-level summary:
- Focus this week: finalize quantization sweep for 7B family, run eval battery on quantized checkpoints, unblock onboarding for customer-model X-7B-v2.
- Small wins: 4-bit QAT baseline converged on small eval set; observed 1.4% avg EM drop vs FP16 for standard QA tasks after calibration.
- Major blocker: intermittent tokenization mismatch with model X tokenizer causing occasional length discrepancies in eval harness.

Agenda:
1) Standups / short updates
2) Quantization experiments (post-training vs QAT)
3) Evals: battery, metrics, regression alerts
4) Model onboarding status for customer X-7B-v2
5) Action items / next steps

1) Standup updates (by person):
- Aisha: Coordinated quant sweep infra; landed automated metric reporter that uploads per-checkpoint eval summaries to s3. Started a run of PTQ (GPTQ-style) 4-bit + per-channel quantization on X-7B-v2; scheduled overnight jobs for variable sequence lengths (128, 512, 1024).
- Liam: Working on eval harness fixes (tokenization edge cases). Found root cause: tokenizer config missing special-case for byte-level BOM in a subset of customer data; patch in PR #789. Running regression tests across 12 datasets.
- Sofia: Did early QAT prototype (LoRA + 4-bit simulated quant) on smaller proxy dataset. Training lamped for 18 hours, gave promising perplexity/ROUGE tradeoffs; preparing logs for review.
- Diego: Benchmarking runtime performance for quantized kernels on A100 vs H100. Observed that for batch sizes <8, 4-bit paths using fused-kernel show ~1.8x throughput improvement and ~22% reduction in p99 latency vs FP16. Need to validate with KV cache enabled.
- Noor: Hooked cost and latency dashboard to quant sweep pipeline. Noticing higher variance for long-seq jobs; adding more traces to per-token latency breakdown.

2) Quantization experiments:
- Experiments running: PTQ-4bit-per-channel, PTQ-8bit, QAT-4bit (LoRA adapter), and mixed-precision (int8 weights + fp16 activations).
- Preliminary results:
  * PTQ-4bit-per-channel (symmetric) on X-7B-v2: average task accuracy drop ~1.4% on QA suite, small decline on summarization (ROUGE-L -0.9). Latency and memory improvements meet Dedicated cost targets.
  * PTQ-8bit: negligible metric impact, modest memory savings; likely safe default for hosted API.
  * QAT-4bit (LoRA): closes ~60% of gap vs PTQ-4bit on QA metrics but requires ~20% more fine-tune compute; promising for high-SLA customers who want max cost savings.
- Observations / notes:
  * Calibration dataset matters a lot for PTQ; using in-domain calibration from customer X reduced drop by ~0.6% vs generic wiki-style corpus.
  * Per-channel symmetric quantization worked better than per-tensor for attention weights.
  * We need automated checks so we don't roll PTQ-4bit to Hosted unless it meets a per-customer tolerance threshold.

3) Evals and regression tracking:
- Eval harness: running the standard battery (QA, summarization, instruction-following, toxic content check, safety prompts) plus regression tests derived from customer-critical prompts.
- New metric reporting: per-checkpoint delta vs baseline FP16, and a synthetic "quality score" combining accuracy + safety penalties. These are uploaded to: s3://redwood-ml-quant/evals/2026-04-28/X-7B-v2/
- Tokenization mismatch: some eval failures (off-by-one tokens) traced to tokenizer variant used by the customer when exporting model weights. Action: add tokenizer auto-detection step to onboarding script and surface a warning in Console.
- Regression alerting: configure Optimize to raise alert if quality_score drops >2% vs baseline for any major task. Liam to add alerts for nightly runs.

4) Model onboarding status (customer X-7B-v2):
- Steps completed: model artifact ingestion, initial compatibility check, conversion to internal format, baseline FP16 eval, quant sweep triggered.
- Blockers: tokenizer mismatch (see above); also a missing config flag for attention-cache layout in the exported model (PR filed: JIRA-APPL-321).
- Security / compliance: customer requested key-rotation policy for private deployment; security team provided KMS integration checklist — Diego to follow up with infra.
- SLA discussion: product wants to present tuning options (PTQ-8bit default, paid QAT-4bit) for Dedicated customers. Needs pricing input from finance.

5) Action items / owners:
- Liam: finish tokenizer auto-detect + patch in PR #789; add regression alerting thresholds to nightly job. (ETA: 2026-04-30)
- Aisha: run second calibration sweep using customer-specific calibration set; compare per-dataset deltas and prepare short report. (ETA: 2026-05-01)
- Sofia: expand QAT experiments to full training dataset for one checkpoint; evaluate compute cost vs quality gains and document recommended LoRA hyperparams. (ETA: 2026-05-04)
- Diego: run KV-cache enabled throughput tests on H100 for the winning PTQ checkpoint and report p50/p95/p99. (ETA: 2026-04-30)
- Noor: add per-token tracepoints to dashboard for long-seq jobs and tune visualization for easier triage. (ETA: 2026-05-03)

Open questions / discussion points to bring next week:
- Thresholds for automatic promotion of quantized checkpoints to Hosted pool (per-model + per-customer fallback policy). Proposed: require quality_score >= 98% of baseline and no safety regressions.
- Cost/benefit for offering QAT as managed service vs recommending customers run in-house. Need an estimate of average extra compute and expected price premium.
- How to surface tokenizer/format mismatches in Console to reduce manual interventions during onboarding.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep an eye on mixed-precision int8+fp16 hybrid — might be the best tradeoff for Hosted.
- Capture a short how-to for customers: "Why your model may behave slightly different after PTQ and how we calibrate" — Aisha draft due next week.
- Link related artifacts: Confluence quantization playbook + PR #789 + JIRA-APPL-321 for attention-cache fix.

Appendix: quick results table (short):
- FP16 baseline (X-7B-v2): QA accuracy 78.3, ROUGE-L 43.1
- PTQ-8bit: QA 77.9 (-0.4), ROUGE-L 42.9 (-0.2)
- PTQ-4bit-per-channel: QA 76.9 (-1.4), ROUGE-L 42.7 (-0.4)
- QAT-4bit (LoRA): QA 77.5 (-0.8), ROUGE-L 42.9 (-0.2)

End of notes.
